title: 15 Financial Traps Disguised as Good Decisions
description:
The most dangerous money mistakes don't look like mistakes. In this video I go through 15 financial traps disguised as good decisions, from three angles: the math traps (the house you're approved for, the big tax refund), the emotional traps (co-signing, lending to family, timeshares) and the long-term traps (company stock, raiding your 401k), plus a 7-question filter to catch any trap before you step in.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

0:00 Intro
1:29 How we got the numbers
1:57 Angle 1: The Numbers
2:01 1. The biggest house you're approved for
3:43 2. Paying off a cheap mortgage first
5:12 3. Keeping everything in savings
6:42 4. Buying because it's on sale
8:07 5. Extended warranties
9:32 6. The big tax refund
10:51 Angle 2: The Psychology
10:56 7. Any degree at any cost
12:32 8. Co-signing a loan
13:57 9. Lending to friends and family
15:13 10. The timeshare
16:31 11. You deserve it
17:44 12. Keeping up appearances
18:55 A quick favor
19:11 Angle 3: The Playbook
19:20 13. Loading up on your company's stock
20:47 14. Raiding your 401(k) to pay off debt
22:29 15. Paying for college before retirement
23:53 Why smart people fall for them
25:25 The trap filter
26:54 Three traps in real life
28:46 Questions people ask
31:24 Recap: all 15 traps
32:10 What to do next

Sources:
- Federal Reserve, Consumer Credit G.19 (student loans outstanding above $1.6 trillion)
- IRS, retirement plan early distributions (10% additional tax before 59 1/2, with exceptions); IRS Tax Withholding Estimator
- Federal Trade Commission, Cosigning a Loan (required cosigner notice); FTC guidance on timeshare resale scams
- U.S. Department of Education, College Scorecard
- Enron collapse (2001): employee 401(k) concentration in company stock, as widely reported
- Growth and inflation figures: stated illustrative math
